# Radio

Radio — single option within a named radio group. Supports controlled (`isChecked`) and uncontrolled (`defaultChecked`) usage. Built on Base UI's Radio, wrapped in `FieldFrame` (A7) for the label and the description caption. Base UI's Radio has no standalone `checked` prop — selection lives on a `RadioGroup` ancestor. `RadioGroup` renders one real, shared Base UI `RadioGroup` around all of its options and passes each one `grouped`, so the group gets Base UI's native roving-tabindex keyboard nav across options for free, same as `ChoiceGrid`'s radio-type rows. A `Radio` used on its own (no `grouped`, the default) — a lone question, a `ChoiceGrid` cell, or sibling Radios sharing a bare `name` the way the "Group" story composes them — owns a private, single-item group instead, so it stays independently controllable exactly like the native input it replaces. That private group keeps its own `role="radiogroup"` (axe rejects `aria-readonly`/ `aria-required` on a role-less `div`) but drops the `aria-labelledby` it would otherwise inherit from an ambient Fieldset legend it has no business naming itself after.

**Import:** `import { Radio } from '@/components';`

## Usage

Use `Radio` directly only when options need custom layout, such as radio cells inside a table.

Make one option the default: the safest and lowest-risk one. If a person may decline all options, add a "None" option; if the list cannot be complete, add "Other".

## Motion

Radio reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Mark and fill change color. |

## Alternatives

- For a standard radio question with a shared legend and error, use `RadioGroup`.
- For a question where several options may be chosen, use `CheckboxGroup` or `Checkbox`.
- For a list of six or more options, use `Select`.
- For a setting that turns on or off immediately, use `Toggle`.

## Best practices

### Reserve choice tiles for one big question with two to four pictured options. {#reserve-choice-tiles-for-one-big-question-with-two-to-four-pictured-options}

Use `appearance="tile"` when a step asks one focal question with two to four options and every option carries an `illustration`. Keep ordinary form lists and sets of five or more options in `plain` or `card`.

Do: Two pictured tiles for one focal question.
Don't: Plain text options without illustrations drawn as tiles.

### Show one answer selected at a time. {#show-one-answer-selected-at-a-time}

A radio group holds exactly one answer. Never show two selected.

Do: One radio selected in the group.
Don't: Two radios selected at once.

### Never preselect a high-risk answer. {#never-preselect-a-high-risk-answer}

Leave consequential choices, such as ones about privacy or payment, for the
person to make on purpose. When an option starts selected, make it the safe
one.

Do: The safe option, Keep my history, starts selected.
Don't: The high-risk option, Delete my history, starts selected.

### Keep labels short and parallel. {#keep-labels-short-and-parallel}

Short labels scan as a list; long ones wrap and blur the choices.

Do: Short, parallel labels.
Don't: Long labels that wrap, beside a one-word one.

### Order options by likelihood or risk. {#order-options-by-likelihood-or-risk}

Do: Order options from most to least likely, or from least to most risk.
Don't: Alphabetical order cannot be localized and says nothing about which option fits most people.

### A lone Radio is not a group. {#a-lone-radio-is-not-a-group}

Radios that share a `name` are one group; each option gets its own id. ARIA allows `aria-readonly` on a radiogroup and not on a radio, so a read-only question belongs in RadioGroup, which announces it.

### Avoid long lists and overlapping ranges. {#avoid-long-lists-and-overlapping-ranges}

For six or more options, use `Select`. Do not write numeric options that overlap (`0–20`, `20–40`) or skip a number.

### Keep extra detail in `description`. {#keep-extra-detail-in-description}

`description` renders under the label and is read after the name.

### Let a `Radio` label longer than its line wrap. {#let-a-radio-label-longer-than-its-line-wrap}

The circle keeps its size at the top of the row, and the label is never clipped. See [Overflow](?path=/docs/patterns-states-overflow--docs).

## Accessibility

- **Unique ids.** Each instance derives its own id so labels never resolve to the first radio of the group; pass `aria-label` only when there is no visible label.
- **Required or invalid group.** Include an error message, for example "Select an option".
- **Disabled options.** Disable an option only for something the person can fix on the same screen, and put the reason in `description` at full contrast, never a tooltip; a disabled option leaves the tab order. For a choice that must stay reachable, keep it enabled and use validation, so a screen reader user hears why it cannot be chosen. See [Disabled](?path=/docs/patterns-states-disabled--docs).
- **Keyboard.** Arrow keys move between radios that share a `name`. Focus is a 2px ring on `border.focused`, 2px off the radio.

## Related

- `RadioGroup`: use when asking a complete radio question with a legend, value and error.
- `CheckboxGroup`: use when any number of options may be chosen.
- `Select`: use when choosing one option from a list of six or more.
- `Toggle`: use when flipping a single setting on or off immediately.

## Parts

1. **Radio.** A 12 circle in `plain` and `card` appearances; visually hidden in `soft` and `tile` while keeping native radio semantics, keyboard navigation, and form submission.
2. **Label.** 14/20 text beside the radio in a 24 row. It names the option. An optional minority marker (`"(optional)"` or `"(required)"`) follows a standalone radio's label in plain text.
3. **Description.** Optional 12/16 text under the label that describes the option. It does not name it.
4. **Appearances.** `plain` draws the circle and label inline; `card` wraps them in a bordered surface row; `soft` draws a `--ds-background-neutral` row without a radio dot (selected row shows `--ds-background-selected`, a 1px `--ds-border-selected` edge, and a trailing `fa-solid fa-check` icon) for the majority selection type in a choice flow while the minority selection type keeps its visible control; `tile` draws a 224px pictured card.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Hovered | Unselected: `--ds-background-input-hovered` with a `--ds-border-brand` edge (or `--ds-background-neutral-hovered` in `soft`). Selected: the hovered step of the selected bold fill (or `--ds-background-selected-hovered` in `soft`). |
| Pressed | No step of its own in plain/card. In `soft`, an unselected row takes `--ds-background-neutral-pressed` and a selected row takes `--ds-background-selected-pressed`. |
| Focused | A 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused`, 2px off the radio (or around the row in `soft` and `tile`), for keyboard focus only. |
| Selected | `--ds-background-selected-bold` fill and `--ds-border-selected` edge; the dot is `--ds-icon-inverse`. In `soft`, `--ds-background-selected` fill, 1px `--ds-border-selected` edge, and a trailing check in `--ds-icon-selected`. |
| Invalid | The unselected radio or tile takes `--ds-border-danger` (in `soft`, both unselected and selected rows take `--ds-border-danger`). |
| Read-only | Full contrast, in the tab order, no hover; an unchecked radio takes the `--ds-background-neutral` fill. Not changeable. In `soft`, the selected row keeps its selected fill, edge and trailing check. |
| Disabled | `--ds-background-disabled` fill, `--ds-border-disabled` edge, `--ds-icon-disabled` dot or check. Out of the tab order. In `soft`, the row takes the disabled fill and edge, with the check in `--ds-icon-disabled`. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Circle fill and edge | `--ds-background-input` and `--ds-border-input`; selected `--ds-background-selected-bold` and `--ds-border-selected`. |
| Circle size, edge width | `--radio-control-size` (12); `--border-width-selected`. |
| Row | `--control-sm` (24); gap `--inline-md`. |
| Label | `--ds-text`, body default. |
| Card | `--radius-control-md`, `--border-width-default` edge in `--ds-border`, `--ds-surface` fill. |
| Soft row | `--radius-control-md`, `--ds-background-neutral` fill at rest; selected `--ds-background-selected` fill, `--border-width-default` `--ds-border-selected` edge, and `--icon-sm` trailing check in `--ds-icon-selected`. |
| Choice tile | `--choice-tile-width` (224px), `--radius-control-md`, `--ds-surface` fill; selected 2px `--ds-border-selected` and `--ds-background-selected`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Write each label as the option: "In person". | A sentence or an instruction: "Choose this if you meet in person." |
| Use sentence case and no end punctuation. | Title case, or a period after the label. |
| Keep labels parallel in length and form. | Mix one word with a full clause. |
| Add "None" when a person may decline every option, "Other" when the list cannot be complete. | Force an answer that does not fit. |
| Say what to do in an error: "Select an option". | "Required" or "Invalid". |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | Id of the radio button, which the label points at. A generated id is used when omitted. |
| `name` | string (required) | — | Form key of the radio group. Options that belong together share it, and it is reported in `onChange`. |
| `label` | node | — | The text that names this option. |
| `value` | string or number | — | Form value of this option, and the `target.value` that `onChange` reports when it is chosen. |
| `isChecked` | bool | — | Controlled selected state. Pair it with `onChange`; when it is set, `defaultChecked` is ignored. |
| `defaultChecked` | bool | — | Whether an uncontrolled radio starts selected. |
| `isInvalid` | bool | `false` | Draws the error state, for an option that fails validation. |
| `isDisabled` | bool | `false` | Prevents interaction and dims this option. |
| `isReadOnly` | bool | `false` | Shows the option without letting the user change it. |
| `labelMarker` | enum | — | Marks the form's minority case in plain text after the label: `required` or `optional`. |
| `isRequired` | bool | `false` | Sets the required constraint (`aria-required`) on a standalone radio. Pair with `labelMarker="required"` only when required fields are the minority in the form. |
| `description` | node | — | Secondary text under the label. It describes the option; it does not name it. |
| `illustration` | node | — | Decorative picture shown above the label when `appearance` is `tile`. |
| `appearance` | enum | `'plain'` | `plain` (default) is a radio beside its label; `card` draws a bordered row; `soft` draws a neutral row without a radio dot; `tile` draws a centered pictured tile. |
| `grouped` | bool | `false` | Set by `RadioGroup`. Not for direct use. |
| `onChange` | func | — | Called with `{ target: { name, value, checked: true } }` when the option is chosen. A radio never reports being unchecked. |
| `onFocus` | func | — | Called with the focus event when the radio gains focus. |
| `onBlur` | func | — | Called with the blur event when the radio loses focus. |
| `onClick` | func | — | Called with the click event on the radio button. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class on the wrapper around the radio and its label. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline style on the wrapper around the radio and its label. |
| `testId` | string | — | Maps to `data-testid`, for test queries. |
